items.title: John Levy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I would be playing with Stuff Smith and with special guest Ben Webster.

ctx.x: Like on any given night, what would you have, in terms of playing? You would be playing with Stuff Smith and down the street . . .

Oh yeah. I would be playing with Stuff Smith and with special guest Ben Webster. Across the street would be Art Tatum playing with his trio, Slam Stewart and Tiny Grimes. Then there would be Bobby Tucker with Lucky Thompson and his group, and all the sidemen were well- named – well-received, well-named musicians of that time period. Practically all of the groups, their sidemen were all-stars. Some even later on went on to have their own groups. Everybody was top-notch in that field. Billy Taylor was down the…

items.title: John Levy interviewed by Monk Rowe, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: He gained more experience with Don Byas, Errol Garner and Ben Webster

ctx.x: John Levy is one of the few figures in jazz who has employed his musical prowess as a performer and a businessman. He was born in New Orleans on March 4, 1912 but grew up in Chicago when jazz was king. His boyhood friends included Milt Hinton and Ray Nance and he took up the violin at age eight, later moving to the bass. Early gigs included work with Earl Hines and Stuff Smith, who brought him to New York in 1943. He gained more experience with Don Byas, Errol Garner and Ben Webster, eventually becoming a member…
Mr. Levy was interviewed in the Caribbean aboard a cruise ship on May 31, 1995 by Monk Rowe.
